articles.title: Indian sports wrap, November 27: Prasad Salap’s four-gold flourish powers Maharashtra’s triumph at Youth Gymnastics Champs - Sportstar
articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 27: Prasad Salap’s four-gold flourish powers Maharashtra’s triumph at Youth Gymnastics Champs Sportstar
articles.content: Chennai GYMNASTICS Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh continued their impressive medal-winning spree at the 1st Youth Artistic Gymnastics National Championships, stamping their authority on Day 3 by clinching the Grade 9 Out-Age and In-Age team titles, respectively, at INS Hamla, Malad. Maharashtra produced a commanding display of precision, power and consistency to top the Grade 9 Out-Age team standings with 177.400 points. Uttar Pradesh put up a spirited challenge to finish runners-up with 173.199, while West Bengal secured third place with 154.035. Maharashtra’s Prasad Santosh Salap was the standout performer in the Out-Age category, combining technical finesse with remarkable execution to capture the individual all-around crown with 63.633 points. His teammate Aadesh Waghchoude delivered a strong performance to finish second with 61.501, while Services’ Ayush Nath claimed third place with 60.900. Prasad further underlined his dominance in the apparatus finals, displaying exceptional control, strength and composure to sweep four gold medals. He topped the Pommel Horse, Still Rings, Parallel Bars and Horizontal Bar events, showcasing his versatility across the apparatus. Haryana’s Ritik impressed with his floor routine to claim the Floor Exercise title, while Services’ Tushar Khanra emerged victorious in the Vault. In the Grade 9 In-Age competition, Uttar Pradesh produced an equally impressive team performance, accumulating 194.533 points to secure the championship. Services finished a close second with 185.466, narrowly edging Odisha (GFI-2), who finished third with 185.366. Maharashtra’s Jeet Santosh Chavan delivered a polished all-around performance, blending fluid transitions, assured landings and technical precision to clinch the individual title with an impressive 67.034 points. Uttar Pradesh’s Yatharth Kesharwani finished second with 65.634, while his teammate Kush secured third place with 65.533 in a closely contested battle. Jeet continued his golden run in the apparatus finals, displaying excellent rhythm and control to capture the Floor Exercise and Pommel Horse titles. Yatharth showcased his strength and execution to top the Still Rings and Horizontal Bar, while Uttar Pradesh’s Ujjwal Kumar Pandit produced a commanding Parallel Bars routine to claim gold. Karnataka’s Sai Daksh Mohan Kadam rounded off the apparatus champions by topping the Vault. - Team Sportstar SQUASH Ayaan Vaziralli wins Qatar Challenger squash India’s Ayaan Vaziralli clinched his maiden PSA Tour title at the QSF 5 Challenger squash in Doha on Thursday. Top seed Vaziralli from Mumbai, ranked 173 in the world, rallied to defeat Egyptian fourth seed Hassan Menshawy 7-11, 11-7, 11-9, 11-2 in the final. Vaziralli was a quarterfinalist in the National championship held in Mumbai last week. - Team Sportstar

articles.title: Was Siraj crying after 2nd Test snub? Ex-India spinner wonders on live TV - India Today
articles.summary: Was Siraj crying after 2nd Test snub? Ex-India spinner wonders on live TV India Today
articles.content: Former India spinner Murali Kartik wondered if Mohammed Siraj was in tears after the pacer was left out of India's playing XI for the second Test against New Zealand in Christchurch on Friday. Siraj, one of India's leading wicket-takers in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle, has now missed out in two successive Tests, with Kartik questioning the decision to leave him out again.India vs New Zealand 2nd Test, Day 1: UPDATES | SCORECARDSiraj was dropped for the first Test in Wellington last week, with India opting for Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep, Anshul Kamboj and Prasidh Krishna in their pace attack. The match ended in a draw after India's bowlers failed to take all 20 New Zealand wickets.There was no place for Siraj in Christchurch either. Captain Shubman Gill handed Gurnoor Brar his Test debut in place of Krishna, leaving the Hyderabad pacer out for a second straight match. It is the first time in six years since his Test debut that Siraj has failed to play a match in a Test series.During the broadcast after the toss, Siraj was seen walking around in sunglasses. The visuals caught Kartik's attention, with the former spinner wondering if the 32-year-old was finding it difficult to deal with another snub."Is he crying? Because he is an emotional person. Some people are fine even when they are dropped, but some really want to play. They don't care if they have pain in their feet or a headache; they will give it everything. Siraj is like that," Kartik said on Sony Sports."Sometimes you hide the hurt you are feeling because he was dropped even in the ODIs. Even against the West Indies, he played only as an afterthought. This hurts a player. Why even pick him in the squad and take him to New Zealand if you feel his form isn't good or if he isn't bowling well in the nets?" he added.Kartik wasn't the only former India player to question the decision. Sunil Gavaskar also felt Siraj's omission was tough on the pacer, while bringing Ravindra Jadeja into the discussion."You're talking about Siraj. What about Jadeja? I do believe that his spin would have been pretty useful on the fourth and fifth days because he gives the ball a fair tweak. He's not somebody who will toss the ball up, but he's known to get the ball to grip and turn, even on the most placid of pitches," Gavaskar said."So, I think it's tough for him as well as for Siraj. Now, Siraj is among the top wicket-takers in the cycle. So, let's wait and see. The way I've always seen it is that whatever reservations you might have about the XI, the 14 or the 16, once the team is selected, it is your team and my team. It's an Indian team. So, I back this team now that they've picked this playing XI, and I'm praying that this team does well," he added.While Gavaskar said he would back the team picked by the management, Kartik questioned why Siraj had been taken on the tour if there were doubts over his form.After the Wellington Test, Gill had indicated that Siraj's omission was down to his current form, while admitting that leaving out the experienced pacer was a difficult decision. Former India batter Mohammad Kaif also backed Siraj, saying the pacer should be among the first names in the playing XI whenever India tour overseas.Siraj last played Test cricket during India's tour of Sri Lanka in August, where he managed four wickets in two matches.Since then, he has featured in three first-class matches, captaining Hyderabad twice in the Ranji Trophy before taking a four-wicket haul against New Zealand A. He also played just one match in the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, picking up two wickets.- EndsTune InMust Watch

articles.title: Maharashtra makes promotions primary route for senior posts in Government Medical Colleges - Medical Dialogues
articles.summary: Maharashtra makes promotions primary route for senior posts in Government Medical Colleges Medical Dialogues
articles.content: Mumbai: The Maharashtra government has made promotions the primary route for filling senior academic and administrative positions in government medical colleges, narrowing opportunities for candidates from outside the state-run medical education system.Under the revised recruitment rules notified by the Medical Education Department, associate professors with a minimum of three years of experience in their respective subjects will be eligible for promotion to the post of professor. The eligibility criteria for the post of dean have also been tightened. Candidates must have served as professors in government medical colleges for at least five years and possess a minimum of 10 years of teaching experience in a medical institution.Also Read:11 contractual doctors allegedly paid bribes for permanent jobs at Pune Medical College, complaint filedSimilarly, appointments to the post of joint director will be made through promotion. Selection will be based on seniority among deans who have completed at least three years in the position.The revised framework retains a combination of promotion and direct recruitment for associate professor vacancies. Half of these posts will be filled through promotions, while the remaining 50 per cent will be filled through direct recruitment based on recommendations of the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC), BW Education reported. Recruitment to assistant professor positions will continue to take place through direct selection by the commission.The changes have raised concerns over the limited opportunities for experienced medical educators and researchers working outside government medical colleges to enter the state's senior academic and administrative hierarchy.Critics have also questioned the increased reliance on seniority for leadership appointments, arguing that the approach could restrict the entry of candidates with substantial academic, research and institutional experience.The revised rules are expected to reshape career progression within Maharashtra's government medical colleges, particularly for faculty aspiring to move into senior teaching and administrative positions. They also mark a shift towards an internal promotion-based system for filling key leadership posts in the state's medical education department.Also Read:MP medical teachers announce statewide agitation on December 14 over 12-point demands

articles.summary: Maharashtra appoints counsellors in 1,238 colleges to support students from single-parent families Careers360
articles.content: The Maharashtra Higher and Technical Education Department has appointed one counsellor each in 1,238 aided colleges across the state to support students of single mothers and help them continue their higher education without interruption. The initiative, titled ‘Single-Parent Counselling’ (Ekal Palya Samupadeshan), aims to address the financial, social, emotional and academic challenges faced by these students. Higher and Technical Education Minister Chandrakant Patil announced the initiative and unveiled its poster. Under the programme, counsellors will help students understand the difficulties they face during higher education, provide information about government schemes and available facilities, and guide them towards appropriate support services whenever required. Speaking about the initiative, Patil said the counsellors would play an important role in understanding students' concerns and ensuring they receive the necessary guidance and assistance. Three master trainers have been selected from each public university in the state. The selected trainers include associate professors, professors and directors of student welfare. The workshop will cover the challenges faced by students of single mothers, the implementation of recommendations made by the Bagla Committee, sensitive counselling skills and referral mechanisms to connect students with relevant institutions and support services. Following the training, these master trainers will train the counsellors appointed in all 1,238 colleges across the state at the university level. BAGLA COMMITTEE SUBMITS RECOMMENDATIONS A committee headed by Hemlata Bagla has submitted recommendations to the state government after examining the educational and social circumstances of students from single-parent families. The state government has also started a statewide survey to determine the number of such students pursuing higher education and understand their specific needs. Based on the committee's recommendations and findings from the survey, the government plans to develop measures for the overall welfare of these students. Also read Beyond Warana, no takers: How Maharashtra’s cluster university policy floundered [https://news.careers360.com/maharashtra-cluster-university-warana-st-xaviers-college-bajaj-institute-of-technology-wardha-naac-nba-vc-appointment-govt-fund] COUNSELLORS TO PROVIDE ACADEMIC AND EMOTIONAL SUPPORT The counsellors appointed in colleges will serve as a support system for students, helping them address their concerns, access educational facilities and benefit from government schemes. They will also periodically review the difficulties students face during their academic journey and guide them towards suitable assistance. The initiative aims not only to support students academically but also to strengthen their social and emotional well-being, improve their confidence and ensure their continued participation in higher education. The programme is expected to contribute towards creating a more inclusive, sensitive and student-friendly higher education environment in Maharashtra. Senior officials present during the poster unveiling included Higher Education Director Shailendra Deolankar, Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education Director Pramod Naik, Maharashtra Directorate of Art Director Kishor Ingle and other officials from the higher and technical education departments.

articles.title: I'm carefree: Shami not thinking about India comeback, explains Test retirement - India Today
articles.summary: I'm carefree: Shami not thinking about India comeback, explains Test retirement India Today
articles.content: Mohammed Shami has ruled out keeping an India comeback on his mind after retiring from Test cricket, saying he has stopped counting the upcoming World Cups and will focus on playing for Bengal and in the IPL.The 36-year-old, whose last international appearance came in the Champions Trophy in 2025, said he was happy to leave selection decisions to the selectors and wanted to enjoy whatever cricket he had left in him.Asked if the 2027 ODI World Cup or the 2028 T20 World Cup featured in his plans, Shami said he was no longer looking that far ahead."I have stopped counting all these things," Shami said in Mumbai. "Now I am focusing on my game. Whatever they (the selectors) will decide will be better. But from my side, the only thing is to keep continuing, to stay in rhythm, and keep playing at least for the state and the IPL."Shami played the first leg of the Ranji Trophy season before announcing his retirement from Tests earlier this month. He then turned out for Bengal in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT), where their campaign ended with a defeat to Rajasthan at the Wankhede Stadium on Thursday.The fast bowler picked up four wickets in the tournament at an average of 43, having taken 14 wickets in three Ranji Trophy matches at an average of 14. With Test cricket no longer part of his immediate plans, Shami said he now had the freedom to decide which domestic matches he wanted to play.Asked if he would feature in the Vijay Hazare Trophy next month, he was clear about his intentions."Sure, yaar. But the option is that now I can pick and choose which games to play and which ones to leave. There is no pressure at all. But hopefully, it goes well, and I stay fit till the next season and keep playing well," he said.Shami also explained why he decided to walk away from Test cricket despite continuing to feel fit and bowl well in domestic cricket. He said the decision was about managing the demands on his body and moving on to white-ball cricket without any pressure."It felt like the right thing, so I did it. I'm moving well, playing well, so I'll play white-ball now bindaas (carefree). It's not good for the body to take too much load. Now when people don't like my skills [in red-ball cricket], then I'm going to play the white-ball game," he said.There were no regrets about calling time on his Test career, Shami added. He was content with what he had achieved and had no intention of dwelling on what might have been."There is no regret [of retirement]. Whatever is written in your destiny, you will get, and I'm happy with whatever I got. Now I'll keep playing till whatever is in my destiny and enjoy it," he said.Shami's next major assignment will be IPL 2027, after being traded from Lucknow Super Giants to Rajasthan Royals. Until then, he intends to keep playing domestic cricket, although he will be more selective about his appearances.Playing for Bengal also gives him an opportunity to pass on his experience to the younger players in the side. Shami said he wanted to contribute beyond his performances on the field and help the next generation learn from his time in the game."As long as you like cricket, as long as you enjoy it, you should play. That is my motivation, that I'm still enjoying it, and I hope some of the boys learn or pick up something while playing for the state because experience matters a lot," he said.Shami was also encouraged by the young talent on display in the SMAT and hoped some of the players would earn IPL contracts."We got to see a lot of young talent. Hopefully, we'll get to see new faces from this tournament in the IPL auction; there was a lot of new talent and skills. Hopefully, some new guys will come this season," he said.- EndsMust Watch

articles.title: Amdavad's preparedness, 2036 Games legacy; spreading Olympism India's thrust during IOC presentation - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Amdavad's preparedness, 2036 Games legacy; spreading Olympism India's thrust during IOC presentation The New Indian Express
articles.content: CHENNAI: Infrastructure, preparedness, spreading of Olympism, upholding Olympic spirit, sports development and long lasting legacy are some of the topics discussed during a presentation to host the 2036 Olympics on Thursday. And of course, there was no question or discussion about the ongoing Indian Olympic Association election.Amdavad, as Ahmedabad will transform itself into when Commonwealth Games in 2030 in hosted, may also be the city to host the 2036 Olympics – that is if India win the bid. Before that there would be endless discussions and presentations between the IOA, host city and the government before the final name is shortlisted through an election by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) members in 2029 (date not specified). This is the first phase of the discussion and is called the continuous dialogue which is One such discussion centring around Amdavad’s preparedness was on Thursday. The IOA headed by its president PT Usha presented the nuances of India’s bid to the IOC’s Future Hosts Commission along with IOC CEO Raghuram Iyer, Athletes Commission chairperson PV Sindhu and IOC member Nita Ambani. It is just once part of a relentless process India would be going through while competing against Germany, Turkeye, South Africa, South Korea, Hungary and Qatar.Apart from the IOA officials, sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Gujarat sports minister Harsh Sanghavi, sports secretary Hari Ranjan Rao and other officials from the state and centre were present during the close to half an hour meeting..Since Amdavad (Ahmedabad) would be hosting the Commonwealth Games in 2030, the IOA apparently spoke about how those existing venues would be used in 2036. The city will see massive overhaul of its infrastructure for the CWG and would continue until the 2036. The hosts will be elected under IOC’s new Fit for the Future initiative. The Future Hosts Commission is headed by Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic and her team.The IOA’s presentation highlighted Amdavad’s preparedness that included infrastructure and support extended by the city, state and the central authorities to the IOA. “The presentation was on a macro level and it went off very well,” IOA CEO Iyer told this daily. “The discussion centred around sports development and our preparedness. We also spoke about how hosting the Commonwealth Games would leave behind a legacy that could be utilized during the Olympic Games. Existing venues and infrastructure could be used in 2036 as well. We made a strong case.”Iyer also said that there was complete support from the city, state and central government. "This is our official presentation to the IOC and the next phase (strategic dialogue) will begin in around March," he said. .The IOA also presented India’s legacy plan and their thrust towards spreading Olympism and the Olympic movement. It also spoke about the long-term impact of the Games and India's ability to host big-ticket games through multiple international competitions over the last two years.One major area that the Future Hosts Committee would be looking at is the long term impact of the Games and utilization of the venues later. India’s poor record in doping that was flagged as a concern by the IOC when the stakeholders last met too was not touched upon by the commission. However, India did speak about clean sport and their effort to curb the doping menace. Athletes experience and long term socio-economic benefits for communities too would be crucial but what could remain a concern for India would be to shift the dates for the Summer Games to winter. And if it is winter, pollution can be a big concern.What nextBy March 2027: IOC Feasibility AssessmentsMarch 2027: Opening of 2036 Strategic Dialogue by the IOC EB; the Future Host Commission will give strategic support to interested parties and carry out site visits to the proposed host regions and produce a report for the EB.In December 2028, the EB will open a Targeted Dialogue with a select number of Preferred Hosts, who will provide a final response to the questionnaire and a full set of guarantees.The host of the 2036 Olympic Games will be elected by IOC Members at the IOC Session in mid-2029..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

articles.title: Maharashtra govt proposes separate property cards for individual flats | Mumbai news - Hindustan Times
articles.summary: Maharashtra govt proposes separate property cards for individual flats | Mumbai news Hindustan Times
articles.content: Mumbai, The Maharashtra government has proposed issuing separate property cards for individual flats in buildings, recording details of ownership, area, associated rights, mortgages and other liabilities.The move is aimed at bringing greater transparency to property transactions and reducing ownership disputes.Talking to reporters, Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said the proposed system, called the Vertical Property Card, seeks to create an independent supplementary record of rights for every eligible residential or other unit, alongside the existing land records, under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code, 1966.The state government has proposed the Maharashtra Land Revenue Rules, 2026, to provide a uniform mechanism for preparing and maintaining these records, he said.Under the proposed system, a main property record will first be prepared for the building and its common areas, followed by a separate record for each individual flat or unit. Every unit will be assigned a unique identification number.The records will include the unit number, name of the holder, sanctioned area, associated rights and liabilities. Details of the building's sanctioned area, common spaces, open spaces and areas under roads will also be incorporated.Different formats have been proposed for urban and rural areas. In urban land survey areas, formats D-1 and D-2 will be used for buildings and individual flats, respectively. In rural and other areas, formats I-A and I-B, corresponding to Village Forms 7-C and 7-D, have been proposed.Entries in the property cards will be based on sanctioned building plans, relevant certificates and registered documents. For new projects, the commencement certificate issued by the competent planning authority will form the basis, while existing buildings will require occupancy certificates and registered documents.Landowners, promoters, developers, flat owners and authorised representatives of institutions will be eligible to apply for the records.Depending on the nature of the project, applicants will have to submit the original property record, sanctioned building plan, relevant certificates, apartment deeds, transfer agreements or deemed conveyance documents and other registered papers, he said.The proposed system will also incorporate details of bank loans, mortgages, property tax arrears, institutional dues, court-imposed restrictions and government liabilities, based on the applicable procedures and verified information, the minister said.The entire process, from application and information collection to scrutiny, rectification, approval and distribution of digitally signed property cards, will be carried out through an integrated online system.The government has also proposed linking the system with the departments of land records, cooperation, local self-government, planning authorities and registration to facilitate digital exchange of information.In cases of demolition, redevelopment or reconstruction, existing records will be closed or updated in accordance with the rules, and fresh records will be prepared on the basis of newly sanctioned building plans.The proposed framework will also require amendments to relevant laws and rules governing cooperative societies, apartment ownership, municipal corporations and town planning. An interdepartmental committee and an empowered commissioner-level office have been proposed to ensure coordination, according to Bawankule.The draft rules will be published for 30 days to invite objections and suggestions. After examining the responses, the government plans to finalise the rules, undertake pilot implementation and subsequently extend the system across the state in phases.The initiative is expected to make ownership records more transparent, facilitate property purchases, sales and bank loans, improve disclosure of liabilities and encumbrances, reduce property-related disputes and fraud, and ensure that government records remain updated.This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

articles.title: Hockey India League gets lifeline after Sports Ministry intervention, auction on Dec 7 - India Today
articles.summary: Hockey India League gets lifeline after Sports Ministry intervention, auction on Dec 7 India Today
articles.content: "As far as I know, it is not that we are trying to stop Hockey India League or that it will not happen. HIL will definitely happen. I think it should take place in January."These were the words of Hockey India chairman of selectors, RP Singh, on the sidelines of the Men's Asian Champions Trophy. He didn't give away a lot, but confidently said that the league will be back in January next year. The auctions for both the men and women's leagues have been set for December 7.India Today has now learnt that HIL has been given a lifeline to survive, with the sports ministry coming in to the rescue. The future of HIL was in the balance as there was uncertainty amongst teams. Ranchi Royals, one of the franchises that had teams in both men and women's leagues, was expelled after failing to pay the players and the franchise fees.This forced India women's team captain Salima Tete and Savita Punia to plead to the sports ministry to keep the league going. Their pleas were heard as the sports ministry formed a seven-member committee to work on the revival of the Hockey India League, with representatives from the Sports Ministry, Hockey India and HIL franchises. The panel was tasked with examining the league's governance, financial model and overall structure.The move followed a September meeting between Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Hockey India officials and franchise representatives to discuss the league's uncertain future.According to PTI, the committee comprised Sports Ministry joint secretary (Khelo India) Vineel Krishna, Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey, secretary general Bhola Nath Singh and treasurer Sekar J Manoharan. Franchise representatives Alok Sanghi, Mahesh Bhupathi and Divyanshu Singh completed the panel.The committee was asked to prioritise the league's governance and financial framework and submit its recommendations to the ministry within a stipulated timeline.A new framework was formed to incentivise and give equity at the league level to the owners who have been part of the league since its comeback in 2024.According to reports, 60 percent of the ownership of the league was handed to the franchise while Hockey India takes care of the technical and operational matters. However, when India Today reached out to one of the officials of the teams, they failed to comment on the matter as it is still confidential.Bhupathi, who is the CEO of the APL Pipers and part of the committee, said that the idea is to ensure that the league continues to grow as the belief is to make hockey the No.2 sport in India commercially."I think all the owners believe that hockey could eventually be commercially the No. 2 sport in India. So since we have invested a lot of money over the last two seasons, the league has been remodeled now to incentivise and give equity at the league level to a group of owners who have been there since day one."We continue to believe that this league will grow. Obviously, a lot of pieces of the puzzle have to fall together, but I think the owners are committed and we have some big groups like JSW, Vedanta. APL Apollo. So on that are backing the league, and we're looking forward to season three," said Bhupathi to India Today exclusively.HIL SEASON 3 NEVER IN DOUBTWhile there was a lot of uncertainty around the league, the teams that remained firm on having HIL never seemed to waver when it came to their commitment.One of the officials of the teams told India Today that they were always firm in continuing as the league has done wonders for both the Indian men's and women's teams.In terms of the upcoming auction, the men's teams will have a total of Rs. 4 Crore to spend, while women's sides have Rs. 2 Crore.After Ranchi's exit, the league has been reduced to six men's franchises and three women franchises. Reports also stated that the HIL GC team, which replaced UP Rudras, has also been cut loose. This means that star players like Hardik Singh, Manpreet Singh and others will be up for grabs during the auction.However, sources told India Today that work is being done to add a fourth team in the women's HIL.The new development comes as a relief to the players and HI as they can now focus to see the franchises play again from January.- EndsMust Watch
